summary: Kambove territory (Haut-Katanga), the copper-mining belt around Likasi between Lubumbashi and Kolwezi, has no reported territorial armed-group presence. The state controls the whole unit: the PNC keeps order in Kambove town and in the mining towns and villages of Kambove, Kapolowe, Manika, Kilela-Balanda and Panda, with FARDC present in the province. Insecurity is criminal and mining-related: clashes between artisanal miners and police in Kambove (Nov 2024, four dead, police HQ vandalised), armed robberies on the Likasi-Kambove road (2024) and the targeted killing of a geologist and his driver on the Likasi road (May 2026), followed by a police manhunt. Bakata Katanga activity in 2024-2026 was concentrated in northern Haut-Katanga/Haut-Lomami (Mitwaba, Pweto, Bukama, Malemba-Nkulu), not in Kambove.

zones.evidence: Territory HQ under full state administration with a police headquarters; violence is criminal or mining-related (Nov 2024 miner-police clashes that left four dead and damaged the police HQ; May 2026 killing of a geologist on the Likasi road, followed by a police manhunt). No armed group holds any part of the town.

zones.description: Rest of Kambove territory: mining towns near Likasi (Kawama, Lupidi, Kibangu, Ndakata), Kapolowe/Lwisha, Manika, Kilela-Balanda and Panda villages
zones.evidence: No reported armed-group activity in Kambove territory in 2025-2026; Bakata Katanga incidents were in northern Haut-Katanga and Haut-Lomami. Order assumed kept by PNC posts, mining police and customary chiefs, with crime (road robberies) the main threat.
